title: Customer security Q&A: RBAC v2, audit logs, SIEM export
body:
Purpose:
This one-pager is a concise reference intended for customer security questionnaires and quick trust-center copy. It summarizes RBAC v2 concepts, the audit log schema we emit, how evidence automation packages assets for assessments, and options for SIEM export. Use these Q&A snippets directly in RFPs or as the basis for deeper artifact requests.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SOC, InfoSec reviewers, procurement/security engineers.
- Scope: Hosted Redwood Inference control plane and tenant audit streams for hosted/dedicated deployments. Private deployments may have different export mechanics; see linked_artifacts for on-prem packaging.

RBAC v2 — short summary for questionnaires:
- Model: RBAC v2 is role-and-scope based. Roles encapsulate permission sets (API + Console actions). Scopes restrict role bindings to organization, project, or resource groups.
- Core roles: org-admin, project-admin, model-operator, billing-reader, auditor. Roles are extendable via custom role creation for enterprise plans.
- Inheritance and scoping: Role bindings support hierarchical scoping; project-level bindings do not grant org-wide privileges unless explicitly elevated.
- Principle of least privilege: Default workspace templates grant minimal permissions; recommended roles for production are model-operator + read-only monitoring.
- Provisioning integrations: SCIM provisioning via IdP (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace) and manual provisioning through Console/CLI. Group-to-role mappings supported.
- MFA and SSO: Enforced at org-level for console access; API tokens can be scoped and rotated; recommended: require MFA for tactile account admin flows.
- Auditability: All role bind/unbind, policy edits, and custom role changes generate immutable audit events.

Sample Q&A snippets (copyable):
Q: How are privileges assigned and scoped?
A: We use RBAC v2: privileges are granted via role bindings that include a scope (org, project, resource). Custom roles and SCIM group mappings are supported. Role changes are recorded in the audit log and included in SIEM exports.

Q: Can we provision users from our IdP?
A: Yes. Redwood supports SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO. SCIM provisioning can map IdP groups to Redwood roles and can be limited to specific projects.

Audit log schema — high-level design and fields (what we emit):
- Format: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) for export; internal stores use an append-only event store with signing for tamper-evidence.
- Primary fields emitted per event (example names):
  - event_id
  - event_ts (ISO-8601 UTC)
  - actor_id (internal user id)
  - actor_email
  - actor_type (human|service)
  - request_id
  - request_path
  - http_method
  - resource_type (model, deployment, key, project, org)
  - resource_id
  - action (role.bind, model.deploy, api.key.create, login.sso, config.change)
  - outcome (success|failure|denied)
  - outcome_code (http status or internal code)
  - change_summary (free text short description or JSON diff string)
  - client_ip
  - user_agent
  - region
  - latency_ms
  - payload_hash (SHA256 of request payload when applicable)
  - schema_version (e.g. v1)
- Retention & integrity: Hosted customers can choose 90/365/730 day retention tiers. Audit events are written with a hash chain to provide tamper-evidence and stored encrypted at rest (AES-256).
- Access controls: Audit streams are accessible to org-auditors and via dedicated export endpoints; read access is recorded and itself audited.

Minimal audit event example (NDJSON single-line):
{"event_id":"evt_01FZ9X2A","event_ts":"2025-02-15T19:42:03Z","actor_id":"usr_2a9f","actor_email":"alice@example.com","actor_type":"human","request_id":"req_7093","request_path":"/v1/models/xyz/deploy","http_method":"POST","resource_type":"deployment","resource_id":"dep_1182","action":"model.deploy","outcome":"success","outcome_code":201,"change_summary":"deployed model xyz@v3 to prod","client_ip":"203.0.113.45","user_agent":"redwood-cli/0.8.1","region":"us-west-2","latency_ms":123,"payload_hash":"sha256:ab12...","schema_version":"v1"} 

Evidence automation — what we produce and how it helps audit responses:
- Purpose: Reduce manual artifact collection for control assessments (SOC2, ISO27001, customer questionnaire).
- Automated bundles include:
  - Configuration snapshots (RBAC bindings, org-level settings) taken on a schedule and signed.
  - Policy documents (retention, encryption, key management) versioned and timestamped.
  - Operational logs: compilation of relevant audit events for a time window (NDJSON) packaged with manifest and signature.
  - Deployment manifests for on-prem or dedicated customers (infrastructure inventory, AMI/container digests).
  - Test evidence: scheduled smoke test results, synthetic latency/throughput graphs for SLAs.
- Delivery mechanisms: S3-compatible signed buckets, secure FTP, or encrypted attachments via the customer portal.
- Tamper-evidence & provenance: Each bundle contains a manifest.json with digests and a signature (KMS-backed). Bundles are immutable once created; access to bundles is RBAC-restricted and access requests produce an audit event.
- Typical use-case: During SOC2 or customer security assessment, we provide a dated evidence bundle that maps control IDs to artifacts and includes an index for easy reviewer navigation.

SIEM export options — supported integrations and behaviors:
- Supported sink formats: Elastic Common Schema (ECS) JSON, Splunk HEC, syslog (RFC5424), Kafka (JSON over TLS), and raw NDJSON.
- Delivery guarantees: Exports are delivered at-least-once with sequence IDs to assist de-dupe in the SIEM. For mission-critical flows we recommend using our Kafka connector which preserves ordering per-partition.
- Buffering & backpressure: Client-managed pull (Kafka) avoids buffering limits. Push integrations include local buffering with exponential backoff and dead-letter queues to avoid data loss under sustained downstream outages.
- Schema versioning and mapping: Each event includes schema_version and source_id. We maintain a published mapping guide for ECS fields to our audit fields to assist SIEM normalization.
- PII handling: By default audit exports include actor_email and client_ip. We support a configurable export redact policy to omit or hash PII fields if required by policy. Redaction rules are applied at export time and recorded as part of the bundle manifest.
- Security: All transports require TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 recommended). Splunk HEC and Kafka endpoints support token-based auth; mutual TLS is supported for enterprise customers.
- Rate limiting: Tenant-specific export throughput limits exist to protect the platform; bursts are allowed within quota and documented during onboarding.

Customer-facing sample SIEM guidance snippet (copyable):
We can forward audit events to your SIEM in ECS-compliant JSON over HTTPS (Splunk HEC), syslog, or via Kafka. Events are NDJSON; each includes schema_version and sequence_id. We support PII redaction, mutual TLS, and signing of bundles for offline ingestion. Contact solutions-eng@redwood.com to set up connection details and quotas.

Operational considerations and FAQs:
- Q: How long are audit logs retained?
  A: Default is 90 days for hosted; enterprise customers can select 365 or 730-day tiers and export to customer-owned buckets for long-term retention.
- Q: Can we get real-time streaming to our SIEM?
  A: Yes. Kafka and Splunk HEC provide near-real-time delivery; small processing delays (sub-second to low-seconds) may occur depending on region and batching.
- Q: Is exported data signed?
  A: Bundles and scheduled snapshots include a manifest signed by Redwood KMS. Streaming events include sequence headers and per-bundle signatures when snapshotting.
- Q: Do we redact PII in logs?
  A: Configurable. By default we include actor_email and client_ip; customers can request hashing or removal at export time.

Next steps for customers requesting artifacts:
1) Provide the scope (org id / project id), time window, desired retention, and preferred delivery mechanism.
2) Fill short intake form (link in linked_artifacts) or open ticket with customer-success-security.
3) We will produce a signed evidence bundle or configure a SIEM connector; ETA typically 2-5 business days for standard bundles, earlier for scheduled exports.
